questions.text: Is the pushed word included in the CRC and BYTE_COUNT after the INIT? (Scenario: In the same clock cycle the host writes CTRL bit 0 = 1 (INIT) and a PUSH4 of 0xDEADBEEF is presented.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: No. INIT wins over a PUSH4 or PUSH_N in the same clock, so the push is dropped. The pushed word is not included in the CRC, BYTE_COUNT or BUSY_CYCLES. After INIT the CRC state is the start value, BYTE_COUNT is 0 and BUSY_CYCLES is 0.
questions.evidence: - INIT written takes effect in the clock after the write and clears CRC state, BYTE_COUNT and BUSY_CYCLES; it wins over a PUSH4 or PUSH_N in the same clock (the push is dropped).

questions.text: What does BUSY_CYCLES read: 16 or 17? (Scenario: After INIT, 65 bytes are sent as 16 PUSH4 words plus a PUSH_N with TAIL_LEN=1.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: 17. The 16 PUSH4 words each count one busy cycle, and the PUSH_N with TAIL_LEN=1 also counts one because N>0. Only a PUSH_N with N=0 would not count.
questions.evidence: - BYTE_COUNT is 32 bits and wraps. BUSY_CYCLES counts one per clock in which a push is processed (PUSH4 or PUSH_N with N>0), it is 32 bits and wraps; a PUSH_N with N = 0 does not count.

questions.text: What does BYTE_COUNT read afterwards (decimal)? (Scenario: BYTE_COUNT is at 0xFFFFFFFF and one more byte is pushed via PUSH_N TAIL_LEN=1.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: 0 (BYTE_COUNT is 32 bits and wraps, so 0xFFFFFFFF plus 1 byte reads 0)

questions.text: What 32-bit value does the CRC register read (as hex integer in decimal is fine)? Is it 0x00000000? (Scenario: After reset, INIT is written (CTRL bit 0 = 1) and no PUSH4 or PUSH_N follows. The CRC register is then read.) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?
questions.answer: Yes, the CRC register reads 0x00000000 (decimal 0). INIT resets the CRC state to the start value 0xFFFFFFFF internally, and the final XOR is applied on read, so with no bytes pushed the read gives 0xFFFFFFFF ^ 0xFFFFFFFF = 0x00000000.
questions.evidence: INIT written takes effect in the clock after the write and clears CRC state, BYTE_COUNT and BUSY_CYCLES; it wins over a PUSH4 or PUSH_N in the same clock (the push is dropped).
